title: TimesFM-3: A zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
note: Fetched. Google Research post by two of the authors. 330M parameters, pretrained on over a trillion real and synthetic points. Takes several targets, past-only covariates and covariates known into the future (weather forecasts are named as an example) with no fine-tuning. Masked horizon patches are filled in one forward pass; 9 quantiles from 10% to 90%.

title: TimesFM-3: A zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
note: Fetched. Benchmark claim: best average rank among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME, for point and probabilistic metrics, against Chronos-2, the Toto 2.0 family and TimesFM-2.5; the univariate mode already matches or beats them. Shown as rank plots only: no score table, no load or energy case, no forecast horizon stated. Available on GitHub, Hugging Face and BigQuery.

title: google-research/timesfm repository README
note: Fetched. TimesFM 3.0 is the current version: native multivariate forecasting with past-only and past-and-future covariates. States rank 1 on fev-bench (100 tasks), rank 1 on TIME (50 datasets, 98 tasks) and rank 1 among foundation models on GIFT-Eval. Code is Apache-2.0; the 3.0 weights are non-commercial and non-production when self-hosted, commercial use only through Google Cloud services.

title: google-research/timesfm repository README
note: Fetched. Usage: timesfm3 package, predict_batch takes past_only_covariates (context length) and past_future_covariates (context plus horizon). Contexts beyond 15,360 points are truncated. An MLX backend for Apple silicon is numerically matched to PyTorch; horizons of 128 and more stitch several 64-step output patches. Timings given only for an M4 Max with MLX, not CPU PyTorch.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
note: Fetched (also a research source). Independent study, one university building in The Hague, hourly kWh, 24 h ahead, 57 test days (2 Feb to 30 Mar 2024), observed weather. TimesFM 3.0 with covariates MAE 19.97 kWh, target-only 20.01, TimesFM 2.5 21.07, XGBoost with the same covariates 22.45, weekly seasonal naive 35.27. Publication date not on the page; the arXiv id is October 2026.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
note: Fetched. Covariates help on holidays and slightly hurt on workdays and weekends, so pooled MAE barely moves; RMSE drops from 32.45 to 30.26. A paired daily bootstrap does not separate TimesFM from XGBoost on MAE. Selected context 8,760 hours. Swapping station weather for ERA5 or archived IFS changes MAE by at most 0.17 kWh. Code and data are promised, not yet released.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
note: Fetched (also a research source). Independent, pre-registered simulation: 7,200 series from nine known processes, 12-step horizon, univariate only. TimesFM-3 is never worse than 1.31 times the best method in a scenario, but automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% more accurate on seasonal ARIMA data with four or more cycles. Covariate and multivariate paths were not tested. Publication date not on the page.
